title: Cover Letter - Nicolas Wajs - AI Engagement Manager - Allianz Technology
author: Nicolas Wajs

elements.text: I'm writing to apply for the AI Engagement Manager role in the AI Factory's AI Use Case Delivery team at Allianz Technology. The brief here is unusual in a good way: it's not a technical delivery role and it's not a pure account-management role, it's the discipline of turning a real Operating Entity pain point into a funded, scoped, de-risked engagement, then staying accountable for it through build and beyond go-live. That's the exact seam I've worked in across financial services for most of my career.

At Finastra, I led discovery and solution design across a large portfolio of international financial institutions, working directly with Heads of IT and regional leadership to translate business pain into deliverable roadmaps and to keep competitive, multi-stakeholder bids moving — the same kind of demand-shaping and stakeholder ownership this role calls for, just inside a vendor-to-institution relationship rather than a factory-to-OE one. At Opensee, I owned the relationship with our first cloud and first asset-manager client from onboarding onward, which meant staying the accountable face of the engagement well past the initial rollout, not handing it off and moving on. More recently, I took presales leadership on an early-stage GenAI data platform built specifically for insurance companies, sitting with the OE's actual problem before any build started and shaping it into something a technical squad could execute and a regulated buyer could trust — the same motion this role runs on repeat, across multiple OEs in parallel.

What draws me to this specific role is the "half-pizza squad" model and the idea that one OE's solution becomes the next OE's head start — it rewards exactly the pattern-transfer instinct I've built moving between institutions and verticals over the years. I've backed that instinct with structured AI/ML upskilling (Ecole Polytechnique AI for Business, LangChain/RAG, agentic frameworks, Dataiku) so I can engage the Forward Deployed Engineers as a genuine technical counterpart, not just a relationship layer above them.

I'd welcome the chance to discuss how this combination — regulated financial-services delivery, hands-on AI productization, and comfort owning an engagement from demand-shaping through handover — could plug into the AI Factory's current pipeline of OE engagements.
